segments.title: A look at Cutty Sark's rigging
segments.body: The visit pauses for a look at Cutty Sark's rigging and an appreciation of these sailing ships. The discussion then turns to tea chests and the importance of speed in transporting cargo.

evidence.note: Cutty Sark's visible rigging as evidence of these ships' remarkable construction.

segments.summary: Cutty Sark's rigging provides a brief introduction to the sailing clipper before the discussion turns to cargo packaging and speed.

segments.title: Tea chests and standardised cargo
segments.body: The comparison credits tea chests with the first worldwide standardisation of a transport box, made on a mass scale to carry goods. Wool had already used a degree of standardisation through wrapping, so the distinction concerns the use of a box. The parallel with modern intermodal containers concerns standardised packaging; the brief comparison does not trace a direct line of development between them. Tea clippers combined the transport of these goods with an emphasis on speed.

evidence.note: Tea chests credited as the first transport boxes standardized worldwide and compared with modern intermodal containers, although wool wrapping had already provided some standardization.
He links mass-scale standardized goods transport to the speed-focused role of tea clippers.

segments.summary: The tea-chest discussion links worldwide cargo standardisation to clipper speed and compares boxes with wool wrapping and modern intermodal containers.
